title: The Pile: An 800GB Dataset of Diverse Text for Language Modeling
measurement_description: The paper measured word co-occurrences and average sentiment associated with specific religious terms to identify and document potential biases present in the components of the dataset (The Pile). This was done to understand biases that language models trained on this dataset might pick up.
findings: The analysis found that over the entire dataset, the term 'Buddhist' had the highest average sentiment co-occurrence, followed by 'Hindu', 'Christian', 'Atheist', and 'Muslim'. 'Jew' had the lowest average sentiment, which the authors hypothesize reflects its historical use as a pejorative. Co-occurrence tests also revealed specific contextual biases depending on the term, such as 'radical' frequently co-occurring with 'Muslim', and 'rational' frequently co-occurring with 'Atheist'.
